note: STAGING ONLY — new PAPER FOLDING nonverbal type (kind: fold). NOT the master bank. Each item: a square sheet folded 1-2 times, one hole punched through the stack; the answer is the unfolded pattern = each punch mirrored across every crease. grid = 4x4 hole slots; cells are {r,c} with r,c in 0..3 (row 0 = top, col 0 = left). folds apply in order to the flat sheet: left/right = vertical crease (mirror left-right), up/down = horizontal crease (mirror top-bottom). The render script derives ansHoles = unfold(folds, punches, grid) and asserts it equals the option marked ansLetter, so the key is machine-verified.

questions.prompt: WHAT DOES IT LOOK LIKE UNFOLDED?
questions.explanation: The fold works like a mirror, so the one hole copies across the crease to make two holes, one on each side.

questions.prompt: WHAT DOES IT LOOK LIKE UNFOLDED?
questions.explanation: Folding top to bottom is a mirror, so the top hole copies straight down to make a matching pair.

questions.prompt: WHAT DOES IT LOOK LIKE UNFOLDED?
questions.explanation: Two folds make two mirror lines, so the corner hole becomes four holes, one in every corner.

questions.prompt: WHAT DOES IT LOOK LIKE UNFOLDED?
questions.explanation: The hole sits next to the center, so its four copies land in a tight block around the middle, not in the corners.
